cases.name: Crystal Renee Grubb
cases.about: Her obituary said, "She loved to hike and explore the woods and loved playing with children. She was a lovely person and was loved by lots of friends. She had attended the House of Prayer in Ellettsville."
cases.narrative: On 10/1/2010, a farmer discovered Grubb’s body as he harvested corn in a field off Showers Road. She had been strangled; there were handprints on her neck.

cases.name: Lauren Elizabeth Spierer
cases.dateDetail: LAST KNOWN ALIVE / SEEN; PRESUMED / LIKELY DECEASED
cases.about: Spierer graduated from Edgemont High School in 2009 and enrolled at Indiana University, where she was studying textiles merchandising. Spierer was active in the Jewish community at IU and had spent the previous spring break planting trees in Israel on behalf of the Jewish National Fund.

cases.name: Hannah Noel Wilson
cases.about: Her obituary said, "Hannah currently attended Indiana University, where she was near completion of her degree in Psychology, and was a member of Gamma Phi Beta Sorority. Hannah was passionate for the LGBTQ Community, and had planned to pursue her career in psychology in this area.  She was also an avid photo taker, specializing in "selfies". She was described as bubbly and fun She lived with her sorority sisters in a house off campus.
cases.narrative: On 4/25/2015 her body was found lying face down about 20 feet from Plum Creek Road, near State Road 45 in Brown County. Her gray shirt was pulled up, revealing her lower back. Shewas found fully clothed, wearing tight black yoga pants and black converse shoes. Prosecutors felt the weapon used to beat her to death was a Maglite flashlight.  Bruises on her hands, and scrapes on her arms and hands indicated she fought with her attacker. The pathologist who conducted her autopsy testified that there was no sign of sexual assault.
